name: Mercurius Marketplace
summary: A managed home-services marketplace for Lee County, Florida, with homeowner, vendor and admin portals.
challenge: Homeowners want reliable local pros without chasing quotes, and good local vendors want work without hunting for leads. Mercurius coordinates both sides, so matching, quotes, jobs, payments and payouts all need clear rules, and the public site must never overstate coverage.

decisions.title: One canonical lifecycle
decisions.detail: Requests, matching, quotes, jobs, payments, payouts, disputes and reviews follow one versioned set of state machines with actor permissions, so no record can be left in an unmapped state.

decisions.title: Payment integrity
decisions.detail: Checkout attempts are idempotent, Stripe webhooks are durable and replayable, and money movements are written to immutable journals. Payments stay in test mode until a separate activation decision.

decisions.title: Invitation-gated booking
decisions.detail: Anyone can browse the catalog and join early access, but booking opens by invitation: requests and checkout are refused for homeowners who have not been admitted.

detail: The public site is live for early access while the rebuilt booking flows move through phased acceptance. It shows real catalog coverage instead of invented scale, and services without an active provider say so.
role: Solo build: I engineered, built, deployed and set up this project.

engineering: Next.js and TypeScript on Supabase Postgres, Auth, Storage and Edge Functions
181 SQL migrations, with role-isolation tests run against a local Supabase stack
Stripe checkout and webhook handling in Edge Functions, tested with synthetic fixtures
Intake forms protected by a honeypot, a fill-time check and per-email and per-IP limits
CI gates for lint, types, unit tests and a repository secret scan
